category_title: Students with speech and learning difficulties
minimal_context: Carles is working on a mathematics activity focusing on proportions and percentages with his interactive group.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please start working on the proportions and percentages activity with your group. You have about 15 to 20 minutes for this task.

STUDENT: I can't do this math problem. There are some words here which are very strange.

TUTOR: Read it again and see what you can figure out.

STUDENT: I don't know how. In primary school I was used to going outside the classroom to receive special attention when I couldn't read the words.

TUTOR: Well, you are in this group now, so just keep trying to get it done.

STUDENT: I still don't understand something because of these strange words. Hey guys, I need help, can someone just give me the solution so we can finish the activity?

options.A: Hold back from providing answers immediately, using careful questioning to respond to student thinking and emphasize conceptual connections.
options.B: Use praise and precorrective statements consistently during the interactive group activities.
options.C: Make students aware that their goal is not just to finish the activity by themselves, but to ensure that the whole group completes the task.
options.D: Use simple language that is mathematically proper to describe the proportions and percentages problems during the interactive group sessions.
